Where we actually are

f8c9e8444b28d0fae536a8869e08669ed64f2f74

The key remaining limitation is still present in the live code. With no -TaskId, generic_selection.py only looks for an existing agent_ready Issue. If none exists it explicitly stops with:

“No validated agent-ready Issue exists. Pass an explicit -TaskId to begin fresh work…”

So our “generic do work” command is currently really a generic resume-work command, not a generic get-work command.

Stage 1 has already been started

There is already a branch:

generic-get-work-stage1-atomic-claims

at:

929877f8b7024de1e0c8fa8d28c35a2559028640

And this is actually good news: it has not been overbuilt. The entire Stage 1 commit adds only an 11-line claim_policy.json. It specifies:

resume_only for now
preferred refs/nsc/claims
fallback refs/heads/nsc-claims
atomic multi-ref, nonexistence-CAS acquisition
exact-SHA CAS release
manual exact-SHA stale-claim recovery

That is exactly the conservative architecture we wanted.

The branch is currently one commit ahead and one behind main, so it needs current main integrated before we continue.

What I think we should build next

Do not build another goal-oriented agent. Do not have Claude select tasks. Do not add decomposition yet.

The normal command eventually needs to mean:

Do work
   ↓
Is there existing actionable work?
   ├─ yes → finish the most advanced work first
   └─ no
        ↓
      deterministically find eligible fresh tasks
        ↓
      atomically reserve task + resources
        ↓
      initialize durable Issue
        ↓
      existing TaskReviewAgent takes over

Claude/Codex becomes relevant after the deterministic dispatcher has selected and reserved the task.

For Stage 1 specifically, I would build only the distributed claim primitive:

candidate task
      ↓
task claim ref
resource claim refs
      ↓
ONE atomic Git push
      ↓
all refs acquired?
  ├─ no → lost race; select something else
  └─ yes → initialize/lease Issue

That solves the concurrency problem without inventing another orchestration framework.

The acceptance test I care about

Stage 1 is done when we can run two processes against a synthetic/bare remote simultaneously and prove:

They cannot both acquire the same task.
They cannot acquire different tasks sharing an exclusive resource.
They can acquire two tasks with disjoint resources.
Partial resource claims can never occur.
Claim release requires the exact claim SHA.
A stale claim is reported, not silently deleted.
Losing a race is an ordinary scheduling outcome, not a pipeline error.
The existing Issue lease remains the long-lived workflow authority after claim initialization.

That's enough. No 40-file subsystem.

Then Stage 2 can be the read-only fresh-task dispatcher, and only after its candidate report looks right do we enable:

.\Pipeline\TaskReviewAgent\Start-GameTaskAgent.ps1 -ExecutionProvider claude

to genuinely mean “find useful work and do it.”

So yes: we should continue where we left off. And I think the correction we made to Claude's design was important—the Stage 1 branch is currently appropriately tiny. Our next job is to implement atomic claims behind that policy, not enlarge the architecture. Ai assisted Game Course - Pytho…

Rather than making the enormous TaskReviewAgent workflow run for every documentation PR, I recommend a small dedicated CI workflow that runs only the new checkout-root policy test on every PR. That gives us actual regression protection without burning the full orchestration test suite whenever someone edits a README.

Run this:

& {
    $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
    Set-Location "C:\NSC\NSC\NoSafeCircle"

    if ((git branch --show-current).Trim() -ne "pipeline/canonical-short-windows-root") {
        throw "Wrong branch."
    }

    $WorkflowPath = ".github\workflows\checkout-root-policy.yml"

    $Workflow = @'
name: Canonical Checkout Root Policy

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  checkout-root-policy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5

    steps:
      - name: Check out exact revision
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Enforce canonical Windows checkout root
        run: python Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/tests/checkout_root_policy_smoke_test.py
'@

    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(
        (Join-Path (Get-Location) $WorkflowPath),
        (($Workflow -replace "`r`n", "`n") -replace "`r", "`n"),
        (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false))
    )

    python Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/tests/checkout_root_policy_smoke_test.py
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Checkout-root policy test failed." }

    git diff --check
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Whitespace validation failed." }

    Write-Host "`n=== FINAL DIFF SUMMARY ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    git diff --stat

    Write-Host "`n=== STATUS ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    git status --short
}

The important thing is that this workflow has no paths: restriction. If six months from now somebody puts the obsolete root into some new operational file we didn't anticipate, the policy test still runs.

After that succeeds, I think we're done editing this migration. Then we can commit it as one coherent change and get back to Stage 1.

How can we skip some of this since this is not a game task, it is a pipeline task. These checks I think are unnecessary for pipeline changes. 

* * *

**ChatGPT:**

Yes. You’re right that the current CI is too coarse.

The important distinction is not “pipeline changes need fewer tests because they’re less important.” Pipeline changes often need more careful testing. The problem is that we’re running tests for unaffected subsystems.

Right now TaskReviewAgent Deterministic Validation triggers when anything under Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/** changes or even when any .github/workflows/** file changes, and then it runs the entire TaskReviewAgent regression suite: Codex supervisor tests, scene-path tests, downstream delivery, production commit/push, human handoff, merge-closeout, durable resume, etc. That is why a one-line checkout-root default change turns into a giant CI event.

The history migration workflow has the same problem at a smaller scale. This PR changed the path string inside Pipeline/HistoryMigration/issue_migration_smoke_test.py and HISTORY_IDENTITY_MIGRATION.md, both of which are trigger paths, so it ran the whole history-identity migration dry-run.

For this PR specifically, I checked GitHub: all three workflows have already finished successfully, so there is nothing left to wait for. We can merge #91 whenever you want.

For future PRs, I think we should introduce a simple deterministic impact tier:

Change type	What should run
Docs / constants / path policy	policy test, relevant local smoke test, compile, TaskGraph validate, whitespace
Localized pipeline subsystem	that subsystem's smoke tests + basic repository validation
Orchestrator/Issue/claims behavior	full TaskReviewAgent coordination suite
Game code / Unity / TaskGraph delivery	game-task/Unity/evidence validation

For this exact PR, the correct suite would have been roughly:

checkout_root_policy_smoke_test
real_checkout_smoke_test
workflow_runtime_smoke_test
compileall TaskReviewAgent
taskcontrol validate
git diff --check

It did not need things like:

Codex supervisor regression
scene-path migration regression
production commit/push test
connected Issue → human handoff
downstream delivery/closeout
merge-closeout repolling
history rewrite dry-run

The safe way to implement this is not a [skip ci] label or trusting “pipeline” in a PR title. That would create an escape hatch. Instead, one tiny CI classifier reads git diff --name-only and deterministically chooses the required tier. A final always-running CI Gate reports success after all applicable jobs pass. Then branch protection only needs that final gate.

That also fits Stage 1 nicely. When we implement atomic claims, the classifier would recognize changes to coordination/claim code and run the strong Issue/resource/race tests, but it still wouldn't drag in unrelated game-delivery tests.

I would keep this small. One classifier, three or four tiers, no new smart supervisor system. The current workflows have clearly accumulated enough tests that impact-based routing is now worth doing.

And because #91 is already green, I would merge the path migration first, then make this CI-routing cleanup as a separate pipeline commit so we don't muddy the migration PR.

--atomic

- working tree

schema version

task ID

source main SHA

Worker identity must be unique per process/run.

RESOURCE CLAIMS

Resource ref names must derive from canonical exclusive-resource tokens using a deterministic
hash.

Do not put arbitrary unsafe resource text directly into Git ref names.

CRASH / STALE CLAIM POLICY

NO TTL AUTO-DELETION.

NO silent stale-claim garbage collection.

If a process crashes before Issue authority is established, a stale claim may remain.

The system must be able to inspect/report the exact:

ref
claim OID
receipt
age/creation timestamp

Repair is manual/exact-SHA-only in Stage 1.

An active process may release its own still-exact claims after a normal initialization failure.

A crashed process gets no automatic cleanup.

MINIMAL ISSUE INTEGRATION

Integrate this claim layer only where needed to protect explicit TaskId Issue initialization /
lease acquisition.

Do not add another supervisor or state machine.

Do not change durable Issue semantics.

Once Issue initialization/acquisition succeeds:

1. re-read the Issue;
2. verify exact worker/lease authority;
3. release the short-lived refs using exact claim OID fencing.

If the Issue already represents authoritative resumable work, preserve the existing durable
Issue semantics rather than creating a second long-lived authority.

Keep the integration small.

TESTS — REQUIRED

Use disposable local/bare Git remotes for deterministic concurrency tests.

Required proofs:

1. SAME TASK RACE
   Two workers contend for the same task.
   Exactly one acquires.

2. SHARED RESOURCE RACE
   Two different tasks require the same exclusive resource.
   Exactly one acquires.

3. DISJOINT TASKS
   Two workers claim different tasks with disjoint resources.
   Both can acquire.

4. NO PARTIAL CLAIM
   Force one ref in a multi-ref acquisition to conflict.
   Verify NONE of the worker's other task/resource refs were created.

5. EXACT-SHA RELEASE
   A worker can release its own refs.
   A stale worker cannot delete refs that have moved to a newer claim OID.

6. STALE CLAIM INSPECTION
   A claim can be reported with exact ref/OID/receipt.
   Inspection does not delete it.

7. RACE LOSS IS NORMAL
   Claim contention produces the normal claim-conflict outcome, not corruption or partial state.

8. ISSUE HANDOFF
   Claim remains held during Issue initialization.
   After exact Issue authority is re-read and verified, claim is released.
   A failed authority verification must not pretend handoff succeeded.

Prefer subprocess/process-level race tests where useful rather than only mocking Git.

TEST GIT REQUIREMENTS

Tests must prove:

- current branch HEAD unchanged by claim commit creation
- working tree/index unchanged
- atomic push behavior
- exact lease fencing

Do not depend on timing sleeps as the sole concurrency mechanism.

**You:**

I want to be able to have as many instances of powershell and tasks running as possible. To do this the orchestrator needs to pick tasks that wont have conflicts with each other when they are done.

* * *

**ChatGPT:**

You do need to worry about it, but you should solve it once inside the orchestrator—not manually every time you open another PowerShell window.

The TaskGraph gives us one major part automatically: dependency safety.

For example:

A → B → C

D → E

If B depends on A, the orchestrator won't start B before A is complete. Meanwhile D could run at the same time as A.

But dependency edges do not automatically mean two tasks can't conflict.

Consider:

NSC-101: Change PlayerController.cs
NSC-102: Add dodge behavior to PlayerController.cs

They may have no dependency relationship at all:

NSC-101    NSC-102

The graph would say both are ready. But running them simultaneously is a bad idea because they'll both modify the same integration surface.

That's what the resource system + claims are for.

The system we actually want

A task should be runnable only when all three are true:

Dependencies satisfied
        +
Exclusive resources available
        +
Task not already claimed
        =
Safe to dispatch

So suppose the TaskGraph says:

NSC-101
resources:
  - player-controller

NSC-102
resources:
  - player-controller

NSC-103
resources:
  - enemy-spawning

NSC-104
resources:
  - ui-hud

You open four PowerShell windows simultaneously.

They could naturally end up like:

PowerShell 1 → NSC-101  [player-controller]
PowerShell 2 → NSC-103  [enemy-spawning]
PowerShell 3 → NSC-104  [ui-hud]
PowerShell 4 → looks for work...
                NSC-102 conflicts with NSC-101
                → chooses another task or reports no safe work

That's exactly the behavior we want.

Stage 1 is a critical part of this

The atomic-claims work we're about to implement solves an important race:

Imagine you launch ten orchestrators at exactly the same time.

Without atomic claims:

Worker A reads:
player-controller available

Worker B reads:
player-controller available

A chooses NSC-101
B chooses NSC-102

💥⁠

With Stage 1:

Worker A:
atomically claims
  task NSC-101
  resource player-controller

Worker B:
atomically claims
  task NSC-102
  resource player-controller

Git accepts exactly ONE.

The loser doesn't fail catastrophically. It just says:

[ROUTE] Candidate NSC-102 lost resource claim
[ROUTE] Recomputing available work

and picks something else.

That is why I'm being annoyingly careful about the Git atomic-CAS implementation. This is the foundation for launching lots of workers.

There is one more thing beyond resources

We also need to think about Git integration/write conflicts.

A resource like:

player-controller

might correspond to several files:

Assets/Scripts/Player/PlayerController.cs
Assets/Scripts/Player/PlayerMovement.cs
Assets/Tests/Player/...

If two tasks have overlapping permitted write scopes, that's another useful conflict signal.

Ultimately I want candidate selection to look roughly like:

for each ready task:

    dependencies satisfied?
        no → reject

    already complete?
        yes → reject

    already claimed?
        yes → reject

    exclusive resources overlap active tasks?
        yes → reject

    incompatible integration/write scope?
        yes → reject

    otherwise
        SAFE CANDIDATE

Then from all safe candidates, we pick one.

This scales quite nicely

Suppose there are 40 ready tasks.

You could theoretically open:

20 PowerShell windows

Each asks:

Give me work.

The workers race against the same claim authority.

You might get:

Worker 1  → Enemy health
Worker 2  → Door interaction
Worker 3  → HUD
Worker 4  → Audio
Worker 5  → Camera
Worker 6  → Loot
Worker 7  → Spell FX
Worker 8  → Save system
...

As long as their dependency and resource footprints don't overlap, they can all work concurrently.

You shouldn't have to assign any of them yourself.

So: graph alone? No.

The distinction is:

TaskGraph dependencies
    answer:
    "Is this task logically ready?"

Resource/write conflicts
    answer:
    "Can this task safely run beside the work already happening?"

Atomic claims
    answer:
    "Which worker gets it when several workers try simultaneously?"

We need all three.

The good news is that we're not discovering some giant missing architecture here. Your TaskGraph already has dependency relationships and resource groups; Stage 1 is explicitly adding the atomic arbitration layer we need for concurrency. The later fresh-work dispatcher should use those facts to choose a safe candidate automatically.

And this actually changes how I think about our milestone. I don't want to stop at two concurrent tasks anymore except as the first test. The design target should be:

Launch N orchestrators, and each independently finds the best safe work it can perform without conflicting with any other active orchestrator.

Then two concurrent tasks is just our first proof that it works—not the architectural limit.

**You:**

What if we have a conflict, is there any option for the orchestrator to deal with it?

* * *

**ChatGPT:**

Yes. The orchestrator should absolutely be able to deal with conflicts — but it should do so in layers, from safest/cheapest to most invasive.

The key idea is:

Parallelize implementation aggressively, but serialize integration carefully.

Even with excellent task/resource definitions, an unexpected conflict will eventually happen. We should design for that rather than pretend the graph can eliminate every possibility.

A good conflict flow would be:

Conflict detected before work starts
Another worker owns the task/resource → don't wait; pick another safe task.
Atomic claim race
Two workers try the same resource simultaneously → one wins, the loser recomputes available work. This is what Stage 1 is solving.
Main changed while the worker was implementing
When the task finishes, fetch current main and try to integrate the task branch against it. If Git can merge/rebase cleanly:
[INTEGRATE] Main advanced
[INTEGRATE] Reapplying task onto current main
[PASS] No conflicts
[TEST] Revalidating affected behavior
No human intervention needed.
Actual Git conflict
Then classify it. Suppose task A changed:
PlayerController.cs
and task B also changed:
PlayerController.cs
The orchestrator should not blindly choose ours/theirs. It can enter the existing repair phase:
[CONFLICT] Integration conflict detected
[REPAIR] Comparing task contracts and both changes
A repair agent can receive:
latest main
task contract
conflicting commit/diff
permitted write scope
tests
the other already-integrated change
and try to construct a combined implementation. Then:
repair
    ↓
compile
    ↓
relevant tests
    ↓
TaskGraph/conformance checks
    ↓
integrate
Repair can't be proven safe
Stop.
[BLOCKED] Semantic integration conflict
The GitHub Issue can move to human_action_required with the exact conflicting files/commits and what each task intended.

That last distinction matters. There are two very different things called a "merge conflict":

TEXTUAL CONFLICT
Git cannot mechanically combine two edits.

SEMANTIC CONFLICT
Git combined them successfully, but the resulting behavior is wrong.

The second one is more dangerous because Git may happily say:

Auto-merging...
Merge made successfully.

while the game is now broken.

That's why successful Git merge != successful integration. Every task merged after concurrent work should run its relevant validation again against the newest main.

I would make the overall model:

             MANY WORKERS
                  │
        ┌─────────┼─────────┐
        ▼         ▼         ▼
      Task A    Task B    Task C
        │         │         │
        └─────────┼─────────┘
                  ▼
            INTEGRATION QUEUE
                  │
                  ▼
            current main
                  │
          ┌───────┴───────┐
          │               │
      clean merge      conflict
          │               │
          ▼               ▼
       re-test          repair
          │               │
          │         ┌─────┴─────┐
          │         ▼           ▼
          │      repaired     blocked
          │         │
          └────┬────┘
               ▼
              main

That architecture lets you have 20 workers implementing simultaneously without requiring 20 workers to merge into main simultaneously.

And there's an even better optimization: if a conflict reveals that our resource definitions were inadequate, the orchestrator can learn structurally from it — not through fuzzy AI memory, but by updating the TaskGraph/resource policy.

For example:

NSC-101 resource: player-movement
NSC-102 resource: player-animation

They repeatedly conflict in PlayerController.cs.

That tells us those resource boundaries may be too narrow. We might introduce:

exclusive resource:
player-controller-integration

for future tasks touching that integration surface.

So conflicts can improve the scheduler.

The order of preference should be:

Avoid conflict
    ↓
Lose claim and pick other work
    ↓
Cleanly integrate against newest main
    ↓
Automated bounded repair + re-test
    ↓
Human handoff

I would not build the repair machinery into Stage 1 right now. Stage 1 should stay focused on preventing simultaneous claims. But once fresh-work dispatch exists, a bounded integration/repair phase using the Issue workflow we already have is the right next capability rather than inventing another orchestrator subsystem.

That gets us much closer to the goal you actually want: open as many PowerShell windows as your machine/model quota can tolerate, and let the system sort out both who should work on what and how completed work safely converges back into main.

& {
    $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
    Set-Location "C:\NSC\NSC\NoSafeCircle"

    $Out = "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\stage1-atomic-claims-post-repair.zip"

    Write-Host "[START] Building Stage 1 review package" -ForegroundColor Cyan

    $CoreFiles = @(
        ".github/workflows/task-review-agent-deterministic.yml",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/claim_policy.json",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/claim_policy.py",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/claim_refs.py",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/real_workflow.py",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/tests/claim_refs_smoke_test.py",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/run_agent.py",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/Start-GameTaskAgent.ps1"
    )

    Write-Host "[READ] Discovering real claim/workflow composition callers"

    $Discovered = @(
        git grep -l -E "RealTaskReviewWorkflow|GitRefClaimClient|claim_client|load_claim_policy|load_claim" -- "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/**"
    )

    $Files = @(
        $CoreFiles + $Discovered |
            Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ -PathType Leaf } |
            Sort-Object -Unique
    )

    Write-Host "[STATE] Files included: $($Files.Count)"
    $Files | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $_" }

    if ($Files.Count -eq 0) {
        throw "No review files were found."
    }

    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Out) {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $Out -Force
    }

    Write-Host "[WORK] Creating archive"
    Compress-Archive -LiteralPath $Files -DestinationPath $Out

    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Out -PathType Leaf)) {
        throw "Archive was not created."
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[DONE] Review package created:" -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host $Out
}

The important pieces are now in the right shape:

GitRefClaimClient.acquire() sends the task ref plus every resource ref in one git push --atomic, with --force-with-lease=<ref>: nonexistence CAS for every ref.
Release is one atomic delete with --force-with-lease=<ref>:<exact-claim-oid>.
Claim commits use commit-tree, so HEAD/index/worktree are untouched.
Production RealTaskReviewWorkflow fails closed while policy activation is pending_capability_probe; it does not silently fall back to Issue-only admission.
Exact Issue handoff checks task, worker, lease_id, state_version, and last_event_id.
Hook/policy rejection remains an operational error instead of masquerading as a normal scheduling race.
Cleanup failure returns lease_acquired_claim_cleanup_required rather than ordinary success.
Durable Issue authority can resume past a stale ephemeral claim without automatically deleting it.
The normal launcher generates a unique worker ID per invocation, and the claim client adds an additional per-run claim identity.
The expanded claim suite covers the review blockers.

def log(text: str) -> None:
    print(text, flush=True)


def client(namespace: str, worker: str) -> GitRefClaimClient:
    return GitRefClaimClient(
        local_repository=repo,
        remote=remote,
        namespace=namespace,
        worker_id=worker,
    )


def clean_namespace(namespace: str) -> None:
    c = client(namespace, "probe-cleanup")
    claims = c.list_remote_claims()
    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for ref, oid in claims.items():
        groups[oid].append(ref)

    for oid, refs in groups.items():
        result = c.repair_stale_claim(
            refs=sorted(refs),
            expected_claim_oid=oid,
        )
        if result["status"] != "released":
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"exact-SHA cleanup failed for {namespace}: {result}"
            )


def concurrent(left, right):
    barrier = threading.Barrier(2)
    values = [None, None]
    errors = [None, None]

    def runner(index, action):
        try:
            barrier.wait(timeout=30)
            values[index] = action()
        except BaseException as exc:
            errors[index] = exc

    threads = [
        threading.Thread(target=runner, args=(0, left)),
        threading.Thread(target=runner, args=(1, right)),
    ]
    for thread in threads:
        thread.start()
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join(timeout=120)

    if any(thread.is_alive() for thread in threads):
        raise RuntimeError("concurrent claim probe timed out")

    for error in errors:
        if error is not None:
            raise error

    return values


def race_until_winner(namespace: str, task_a: str, task_b: str, resource_a: str, resource_b: str):
    for attempt in range(1, 9):
        a = client(namespace, f"race-a-{attempt}")
        b = client(namespace, f"race-b-{attempt}")

        results = concurrent(
            lambda: a.acquire(
                task_id=task_a,
                exclusive_resources=[resource_a],
                source_head=source_head,
            ),
            lambda: b.acquire(
                task_id=task_b,
                exclusive_resources=[resource_b],
                source_head=source_head,
            ),
        )

        winners = [
            item for item in results
            if isinstance(item, ClaimAcquisition)
        ]

        if len(winners) > 1:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"TWO WINNERS in conflicting race: {results!r}"
            )

        if len(winners) == 1:
            loser = results[0] if results[1] is winners[0] else results[1]
            if not isinstance(loser, ClaimConflict):
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"race loser was not ClaimConflict: {results!r}"
                )

            winner_client = a if results[0] is winners[0] else b
            release = winner_client.release(winners[0])
            if release["status"] != "released":
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"race winner cleanup failed: {release}"
                )

            return {
                "attempt": attempt,
                "winner_count": 1,
                "loser_status": loser.status,
                "loser_kind": loser.kind,
            }

        if not all(isinstance(item, ClaimConflict) for item in results):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"zero-winner attempt was not safely typed: {results!r}"
            )

        remaining = client(namespace, "race-inspector").list_remote_claims()
        if remaining:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"zero-winner race left refs behind: {remaining}"
            )

    return {
        "attempt": 8,
        "winner_count": 0,
        "result": "all attempts were safely typed zero-winner contention",
    }


def run_namespace(namespace: str) -> dict:
    result = {
        "namespace": namespace,
        "single_ref_probe": None,
        "multi_ref_atomic": False,
        "exact_sha_fencing": False,
        "same_task_race": None,
        "shared_resource_race": None,
        "disjoint_parallel": False,
        "error": None,
    }

    log(f"[TEST] Namespace create/delete: {namespace}")

    single = probe_remote_claim_namespace(
        local_repository=repo,
        remote=remote,
        namespace=namespace,
    )
    result["single_ref_probe"] = single

    if not single["capability"]:
        result["error"] = "single-ref namespace probe failed"
        log(f"[BLOCKED] Namespace unsupported: {namespace}")
        return result

    log(f"[PASS] Namespace create/delete: {namespace}")

    try:
        clean_namespace(namespace)

        log(f"[TEST] Atomic multi-ref acquisition: {namespace}")
        c = client(namespace, "multi-ref")
        held = c.acquire(
            task_id="NSC-990",
            exclusive_resources=[
                "probe:shared-resource",
                "probe:second-resource",
            ],
            source_head=source_head,
        )
        if not isinstance(held, ClaimAcquisition):
            raise RuntimeError(f"multi-ref acquisition did not win: {held!r}")

        remote_claims = c.list_remote_claims()
        if set(remote_claims) != set(held.refs):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"multi-ref acquisition was partial: {remote_claims} != {held.refs}"
            )
        if any(oid != held.claim_oid for oid in remote_claims.values()):
            raise RuntimeError("multi-ref refs do not share one claim OID")

        result["multi_ref_atomic"] = True
        log(f"[PASS] Atomic multi-ref acquisition: {namespace}")

        log(f"[TEST] Exact-SHA delete fencing: {namespace}")
        wrong = c.repair_stale_claim(
            refs=list(held.refs),
            expected_claim_oid="0" * 40,
        )
        if wrong["status"] != "stale_claim_conflict":
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"wrong-SHA delete was not fenced: {wrong}"
            )
        after_wrong = c.list_remote_claims()
        if after_wrong != remote_claims:
            raise RuntimeError("wrong-SHA delete changed remote refs")

        released = c.release(held)
        if released["status"] != "released":
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"exact owner release failed: {released}"
            )
        if c.list_remote_claims():
            raise RuntimeError("exact-SHA release left refs behind")

        result["exact_sha_fencing"] = True
        log(f"[PASS] Exact-SHA delete fencing: {namespace}")

        log(f"[TEST] Same-task concurrent race: {namespace}")
        result["same_task_race"] = race_until_winner(
            namespace,
            "NSC-991",
            "NSC-991",
            "probe:same-task-a",
            "probe:same-task-b",
        )
        log(f"[PASS] Same-task race never produced two winners: {namespace}")

        log(f"[TEST] Shared-resource concurrent race: {namespace}")
        result["shared_resource_race"] = race_until_winner(
            namespace,
            "NSC-992",
            "NSC-993",
            "probe:shared-race",
            "probe:shared-race",
        )
        log(f"[PASS] Shared-resource race never produced two winners: {namespace}")

        log(f"[TEST] Disjoint concurrent acquisition: {namespace}")
        a = client(namespace, "disjoint-a")
        b = client(namespace, "disjoint-b")
        disjoint = concurrent(
            lambda: a.acquire(
                task_id="NSC-994",
                exclusive_resources=["probe:disjoint-a"],
                source_head=source_head,
            ),
            lambda: b.acquire(
                task_id="NSC-995",
                exclusive_resources=["probe:disjoint-b"],
                source_head=source_head,
            ),
        )

        if not all(isinstance(item, ClaimAcquisition) for item in disjoint):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"disjoint GitHub claims did not both acquire concurrently: {disjoint!r}"
            )

        for owner, acquisition in zip((a, b), disjoint):
            released = owner.release(acquisition)
            if released["status"] != "released":
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"disjoint cleanup failed: {released}"
                )

        if client(namespace, "final-inspector").list_remote_claims():
            raise RuntimeError("disjoint probe left refs behind")

        result["disjoint_parallel"] = True
        log(f"[PASS] Disjoint concurrent acquisition: {namespace}")

    except BaseException as exc:
        result["error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        log(f"[BLOCKED] {namespace}: {result['error']}")

    finally:
        try:
            clean_namespace(namespace)
        except BaseException as cleanup_exc:
            result["cleanup_error"] = (
                f"{type(cleanup_exc).__name__}: {cleanup_exc}"
            )

    return result


for namespace in (CUSTOM, FALLBACK):
    report["namespaces"][namespace] = run_namespace(namespace)

custom = report["namespaces"][CUSTOM]
fallback = report["namespaces"][FALLBACK]


def fully_capable(row: dict) -> bool:
    single = row.get("single_ref_probe") or {}
    return all(
        (
            single.get("capability") is True,
            row.get("multi_ref_atomic") is True,
            row.get("exact_sha_fencing") is True,
            row.get("disjoint_parallel") is True,
            row.get("same_task_race") is not None,
            row.get("shared_resource_race") is not None,
            not row.get("error"),
            not row.get("cleanup_error"),
        )
    )


if fully_capable(custom):
    report["activation_candidate"] = CUSTOM
elif fully_capable(fallback):
    report["activation_candidate"] = FALLBACK

report_path.write_text(
    json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
    encoding="utf-8",
)

if report["activation_candidate"] is None:
    log("[BLOCKED] Neither namespace passed the complete GitHub capability probe")
    raise SystemExit(2)

log(
    "[PASS] Activation candidate: "
    + report["activation_candidate"]
)

This probe was useful. GitHub capability itself did not fail. It exposed one narrow production-format parsing bug.

Both namespaces successfully passed:

create/delete,
atomic multi-ref acquisition,
exact-SHA fencing.

They both failed at exactly the same point: the losing concurrent worker got GitHub's real rejection form:

[remote rejected] (cannot lock ref '...': reference already exists)
[remote rejected] (failed)

and our classifier treated that as an operational ClaimRefsError instead of the expected normal ClaimConflict.  The probe explicitly expects the losing worker to come back as a typed ClaimConflict, so stopping here was correct. 

This is actually a good result for the live probe: refs/nsc/claims is supported by GitHub, and the atomic primitive works. We found a discrepancy between bare-repo Git behavior and GitHub's actual porcelain response before activating it.

REAL GITHUB FAILURE WE JUST OBSERVED

The disposable GitHub capability probe established that BOTH:

refs/nsc/claims
refs/heads/nsc-claims

successfully support:

- atomic multi-ref claim creation

WHY THE CURRENT LOGIC APPEARS TO FAIL

Inspect the actual implementation rather than trusting this explanation.

In claim_refs.py, the classifier currently distinguishes porcelain rejection reasons and separately examines race proof text.

Real GitHub places the exact proof:

cannot lock ref '<EXACT REQUESTED REF>': reference already exists

inside the per-ref porcelain rejection summary/reason.

The other refs in the SAME --atomic transaction can simply report:

(failed)

because the whole transaction was aborted.

Fix the classifier so this exact GitHub behavior is recognized safely.

SAFETY REQUIREMENTS

Do NOT regress the previous blocker fix.

A broad marker such as:

[remote rejected]

must NOT mean contention.

A broad occurrence of:

cannot lock ref

must NOT mean contention.

A generic:

(failed)

must NOT mean contention by itself.

Pre-receive hook rejection, ruleset rejection, authentication failure,
permission failure, unsupported namespace, unsupported atomic push,
transport errors, and other policy/infrastructure failures must remain
ClaimRefsError operational failures.

NORMAL CONTENTION MAY BE RETURNED ONLY WHEN THERE IS CONCRETE PROOF TIED TO
ONE OF THE EXACT REFS THIS PUSH ATTEMPTED TO CLAIM.

Recognize at least the real GitHub nonexistence-CAS proof:

cannot lock ref '<exact requested ref>': reference already exists

Also preserve the exact expected-OID/stale-info CAS proof already supported.

For a multi-ref --atomic push:

- the ref carrying the exact contention proof may be classified contention;
- a sibling rejection reason such as plain "failed" may be treated as a
  neutral atomic-abort consequence ONLY when another exact requested ref in
  that same push contains proven contention/transient proof;
- plain "failed" with no proven race must remain operational;
- any explicit policy/hook/permission/capability rejection must remain
  operational and must not be hidden merely because another line is vague.

Prefer the machine-readable --porcelain per-ref information.

Do not solve this by returning to broad stderr substring matching.

The test should synthesize or otherwise reproduce a failed atomic claim push
where the requested refs are, for example:

refs/nsc/claims/tasks/NSC-991

and porcelain reports approximately:

Prove that this becomes a ClaimConflict with held_by_other semantics.

1. "(failed)" alone is NOT contention.

                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Claude returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }

                        Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 1 activation pass completed" -ForegroundColor Green

                    if ($null -ne $Event.total_cost_usd) {
                        Write-Host "[USAGE] Cost: `$$($Event.total_cost_usd)"
                    }
                }
            }

        $ClaudeExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    }
    finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $PreviousErrorPreference
    }

    if ($ClaudeExit -ne 0) {
        throw "Final activation pass failed with exit code $ClaudeExit. Raw log: $RawLog"
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[VERIFY] Committed policy now reads:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Get-Content -LiteralPath "Pipeline\TaskReviewAgent\claim_policy.json"

    $FinalPolicy = Get-Content -LiteralPath "Pipeline\TaskReviewAgent\claim_policy.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
    if ($FinalPolicy.activation.status -ne "active") {
        throw "Stage 1 policy was not activated."
    }
    if ($FinalPolicy.activation.activated_namespace -ne $ChosenNamespace) {
        throw "Stage 1 activated the wrong namespace."
    }

    Write-Host "[PASS] Stage 1 policy activates $ChosenNamespace" -ForegroundColor Green

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[TEST] Final claim suite"
    python Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/tests/claim_refs_smoke_test.py
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Final claim suite failed."
    }

    Write-Host "[TEST] TaskGraph validation"
    python Pipeline/TaskGraph/taskcontrol.py validate
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "TaskGraph validation failed."
    }

    Write-Host "[TEST] Python compile"
    python -m compileall -q Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Python compile failed."
    }

    Write-Host "[TEST] Whitespace"
    git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "git diff --check failed."
    }

    $ReviewZip = "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\stage1-final-activation-review.zip"

    $ReviewFiles = @(
        ".github/workflows/task-review-agent-deterministic.yml",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/claim_policy.json",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/claim_policy.py",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/claim_refs.py",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/real_workflow.py",
        "Pipeline/TaskReviewAgent/tests/claim_refs_smoke_test.py",
        $EvidencePath
    ) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ -PathType Leaf }

    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ReviewZip) {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $ReviewZip -Force
    }

    Compress-Archive -LiteralPath $ReviewFiles -DestinationPath $ReviewZip

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Final working tree:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    git status --short

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 1 final activation pass finished." -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
    Write-Host "[REVIEW] $ReviewZip"
}

If this reports STAGE 1 READY TO COMMIT, send me stage1-final-activation-review.zip (and the JSONL only if Sonnet reported something suspicious).

At that point we are not doing another design cycle. I’ll check the tiny final diff, then we commit, push, open the Stage 1 PR, let the Core CI run, and merge it. After that, Stage 2 is fresh-work selection—the part that finally makes an idle orchestrator pick a new safe task automatically.

* * *

**You:**

Hopefully that will be easier than stage 0 and 1?

* * *

**ChatGPT:**

Yes. Stage 2 should be substantially easier than Stages 0 and 1.

Stages 0 and 1 contained the ugly foundational problems:

Who is actually authoritative?
Can GitHub Issues safely act as durable workflow state?
Can two processes race without both winning?
Can we atomically reserve multiple resources?
What happens after crashes?
How do we distinguish a real race from Git/network failure?
Does the mechanism behave the same on actual GitHub as it does locally?

That is distributed-systems territory. We just spent a ridiculous amount of effort making the floor solid.

Stage 2 is much more conventional. It is basically:

Give me TaskGraph
       ↓
Find candidates
       ↓
Dependencies satisfied?
       ↓
Already complete / WIP / reserved?
       ↓
Resources compatible?
       ↓
Authorized task shape?
       ↓
Rank candidates
       ↓
"NSC-XXX is the best work to do next"

And initially it doesn't even do the work. Our planned Stage 2 should produce a deterministic, read-only dispatch plan first.

The main tricky parts are policy questions, not low-level concurrency:

Defining exactly when a dependency is dispatch-satisfied, especially needs_testing.
Making "finish existing work first" deterministic.
Ensuring existing open Issues reserve their resources.
Making explicit -TaskId and automatic selection go through the same safety checks, so explicit mode can't cheat.
Making sure an unknown/invalid TaskGraph state fails closed rather than causing the model to improvise.

After that, Stage 3 is basically:

selection
    ↓
atomic claim   ← Stage 1 already solved this
    ↓
create/init Issue
    ↓
existing orchestrator

And Stage 4 becomes:

PowerShell 1 ─→ choose → claim → work
PowerShell 2 ─→ choose → claim → work
PowerShell 3 ─→ choose → loses claim → choose again
PowerShell 4 ─→ choose → claim different resources → work
...
PowerShell N

The crucial thing is that we should not invent another clever AI supervisor for Stage 2. That's where this project has tended to balloon.

The selection algorithm should be boring Python. Something like:

candidates = tasks_that_are_dispatch_ready()

candidates = exclude_completed(candidates)
candidates = exclude_existing_work(candidates)
candidates = exclude_dependency_blocked(candidates)
candidates = exclude_resource_conflicts(candidates)

return rank_finish_first(candidates)

Then the model only gets involved after deterministic code has decided what it is allowed to work on.

So I expect the difficulty curve to look roughly like:

Stage 0  █████████
Stage 1  ██████████   ← hardest
Stage 2  ████
Stage 3  ███
Stage 4  █████         ← concurrency may expose surprises

Stage 4 may uncover another real-world edge case because that's when we deliberately unleash several workers at once. But unlike Stage 1, we'll already have the atomic arbitration mechanism underneath them.

And we're finally getting close to the fun test:

Open several PowerShell windows, run the same generic command in all of them, and watch each one independently find useful non-conflicting game work.

That's the point where all of this infrastructure starts paying us back instead of demanding more infrastructure.

* * *

**You:**

We want the same generic command to be able to do decomposition. 
Is that stage 5?

* * *

**ChatGPT:**

Yes. I would make integrated decomposition Stage 5. And I think putting it after we prove N-worker dispatch is the right order.

The end-state generic command should behave roughly like this:

Start-GameTaskAgent.ps1
        │
        ▼
Is there existing actionable work?
        │
   YES ─┴─► Resume it
        │
       NO
        ▼
Is there a safe concrete TaskGraph task?
        │
   YES ─┴─► Claim it → work it
        │
       NO
        ▼
Is there authorized work that needs decomposition?
        │
   YES ─┴─► Claim decomposition authority
        │
        ▼
     Decompose
        │
        ▼
Validate proposed TaskGraph changes
        │
        ▼
Make decomposition durable
        │
        ▼
Re-enter generic selection
        │
        ▼
Pick one of the newly concrete tasks

So from your perspective there is still one command. You don't need to know whether the next useful action is implementation, resume, repair, or decomposition.

Why I would wait until Stage 5

Decomposition introduces a new type of concurrency problem:

Workers aren't merely consuming the TaskGraph anymore. One of them is changing its structure while other workers are consuming it.

I don't want to mix that problem into Stage 2–4 while we're first proving basic dispatch.

So our progression becomes:

Stage 0
Safety/authority hardening
        ↓
Stage 1
Atomic task + resource claims
        ↓
Stage 2
Deterministic fresh-work selection
        ↓
Stage 3
Automatically dispatch one fresh task
        ↓
Stage 4
N concurrent generic orchestrators
        ↓
Stage 5
Same generic command can decompose work

Stage 5 can reuse almost everything we already built.

For example, imagine the graph contains:

NSC-100
Implement enemy combat system

but that's too large to give directly to an implementation worker.

The generic worker sees:

[SELECT]
NSC-100 is not execution-sized.

[ROUTE]
Decomposition required.

Before the model decomposes anything, we'd claim something like:

task: NSC-100
resource: taskgraph-structure

That prevents two PowerShell windows from independently decomposing NSC-100.

I would probably make TaskGraph structural mutation globally exclusive initially:

exclusive resource:
taskgraph-structure

That means only one orchestrator can be decomposing/changing TaskGraph structure at once.

But importantly:

Worker A → implementing PlayerMovement
Worker B → implementing EnemyAttack
Worker C → implementing UI
Worker D → decomposing NSC-100

can still all operate concurrently.

Only another decomposition worker would be blocked:

Worker E → wants to decompose NSC-200
           ↓
       taskgraph-structure already claimed
           ↓
       pick something else

That's simple and safe. Later we could make TaskGraph mutation more granular if it ever becomes a bottleneck, but I doubt we'd need to.

The model should propose decomposition, not authorize it

This is another place where I want to keep our deterministic/model boundary.

Claude/Fable can intelligently propose:

NSC-100 Enemy Combat

→ NSC-101 Enemy Detection
→ NSC-102 Enemy Chase
→ NSC-103 Enemy Attack
→ NSC-104 Damage Integration
→ NSC-105 Combat Runtime Validation

But Python should verify things like:

IDs valid?
Parent preserved?
Dependencies valid?
No cycles?
Resources declared?
Children authorized by parent scope?
No duplicate work?
Acceptance criteria present?
Task sizes acceptable?
Graph still validates?

Then either:

[PASS] Decomposition accepted

or:

[BLOCKED] Proposed decomposition violates TaskGraph contract

The model doesn't get to scribble arbitrary new canon into our workload.

One thing I would not do

I wouldn't let a decomposition worker create child tasks in its private checkout and immediately begin implementing one before those tasks become durable.

Better:

decompose
   ↓
validate
   ↓
make TaskGraph change durable
   ↓
release decomposition claim
   ↓
generic selector runs again
   ↓
atomically claim a child normally

That way every other orchestrator sees the same world.

And this gives us the experience I think you're aiming for. Eventually you type the same thing into ten PowerShell windows:

.\Start-GameTaskAgent.ps1

and you might see:

Window 1: [WORK] NSC-041 Player health
Window 2: [WORK] NSC-052 Door interaction
Window 3: [WORK] NSC-067 Spell cooldown UI
Window 4: [DECOMPOSE] NSC-080 Boss encounter
Window 5: [WORK] NSC-043 Damage feedback
Window 6: [CLAIM] Lost resource race; selecting again
Window 6: [WORK] NSC-071 Audio transition

Nobody needs to tell the orchestrator which mode it's in.

That's the real final form of the generic command. Stage 5 is where it stops being merely an automatic task runner and starts becoming an automatic work generator + work executor.

    git log --oneline --decorate -6

What I expect

                }
                catch {
                    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Line)) {

                    }

                }

                if ($Event.type -eq "system") {
                    if ($Event.subtype -eq "init") {
                        Write-Host "[AGENT] Claude session started" -ForegroundColor Cyan
                    }
                    elseif ($Event.subtype -eq "api_retry") {
                        Write-Host "[RETRY] API retry $($Event.attempt)/$($Event.max_retries)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "stream_event") {
                    $Inner = $Event.event

                    if (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_start" -and
                        $Inner.content_block.type -eq "tool_use"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host ""
                        Write-Host "[TOOL] $($Inner.content_block.name)" -ForegroundColor DarkCyan
                    }
                    elseif (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Claude returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }
                    else {
                        Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 2 implementation pass completed" -ForegroundColor Green
                    }

                    if ($null -ne $Event.total_cost_usd) {
                        Write-Host "[USAGE] Cost: `$$($Event.total_cost_usd)"
                    }
                }
            }

        $ClaudeExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    }
    finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $PreviousErrorPreference
    }

    if ($ClaudeExit -ne 0) {
        throw "Stage 2 Sonnet pass failed with exit code $ClaudeExit. Raw log: $RawLog"
    }

    Write-Host ""

    Write-Host "[STATE] Changed files:"

                    }
                    elseif (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Fable review returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }

TRANSIENT/OPERATIONAL CLAIM READ FAILURE:

Continue producing a read-only plan, because Stage 3 atomic acquisition remains final arbitration.

But make the plan explicitly provisional.

At minimum:

- claim_observation.status must remain unavailable;
- do NOT pass an active claim namespace + empty map as though inspection succeeded;
- pass claim_namespace=None or an equivalent explicit "not observed" signal into the candidate kernel;
- add one clear plan-level reason explaining:
  Stage 1 claim snapshot unavailable; claim eligibility was not checked; Stage 3 atomic claim remains authoritative.

Do not mark individual candidates as proven claim-free when claims were not observed.

COMMITTED CLAIM POLICY INVALIDITY:

This is different.

If loading/validating the committed Stage 1 claim policy raises ClaimPolicyError or equivalent committed-policy validation failure:

return blocked_invalid_state.

Do NOT downgrade a corrupt committed coordination policy to a transient unavailable claim snapshot.

Add tests for both paths.

============================================================
5. MEDIUM — MALFORMED RESOURCE CLAIM TOKEN
============================================================

resource_claim_ref / canonical_resource_hash can reject malformed resource tokens, including overlong values.

One malformed committed candidate must not crash the whole generic plan with an exception.

Catch the NARROW actual Stage 1 claim-ref validation exception around task/resource claim-ref derivation.

Reject only that candidate with a machine-readable reason such as:

malformed_exclusive_resource_token

or the closest existing naming convention.

Fail closed.

Do not hide unrelated programming errors.

Add a regression test using the real maximum-length boundary.

============================================================
6. MEDIUM — DETECT HEAD MOVEMENT
============================================================

Stage 2 records source_commit, but production helpers currently re-resolve HEAD.

The planner must not silently return a plan assembled from multiple Git revisions.

Keep this fix small.

At minimum:

- capture source_commit at plan start;
- if a TaskGraph state payload reports head_commit, verify it equals source_commit;
- after all production observations are assembled, re-read HEAD;
- if HEAD != source_commit, return blocked_invalid_state or equivalent typed failure;
- do not return a normal fresh_candidate plan after detected source movement.

Do not add repository locking.
Do not fetch/reset/checkout.
Stage 3 atomic arbitration will still handle later staleness.

If existing committed-task helpers can cheaply accept an explicit source commit instead of HEAD, using that is good, but do not rewrite the committed-task subsystem for Stage 2.

Add focused regression coverage.

    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(
        $PromptPath,
        (($Prompt -replace "`r`n", "`n") -replace "`r", "`n"),
        (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false))
    )

    Write-Host "[AGENT] Launching Claude Sonnet for Stage 2 repair" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
    Write-Host ""

    $PreviousErrorPreference = $ErrorActionPreference

    try {
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"

        Get-Content -LiteralPath $PromptPath -Raw -Encoding UTF8 |
            docker compose -p nosafecircle run --rm -T claude `
                claude -p `
                --model sonnet `
                --max-turns 70 `
                --permission-mode dontAsk `
                --output-format stream-json `
                --verbose `
                --include-partial-messages `
                --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write,Bash `
                --allowedTools Read Glob Grep Edit Write Bash `
                --disallowedTools NotebookEdit WebSearch WebFetch 2>&1 |
            Tee-Object -FilePath $RawLog |
            ForEach-Object {
                $Line = [string]$_

                try {
                    $Event = $Line | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
                }
                catch {
                    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Line)) {
                        Write-Host "[RAW] $Line" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
                    }
                    return
                }

                if ($Event.type -eq "system") {
                    if ($Event.subtype -eq "init") {
                        Write-Host "[AGENT] Claude session started" -ForegroundColor Cyan
                    }
                    elseif ($Event.subtype -eq "api_retry") {
                        Write-Host "[RETRY] API retry $($Event.attempt)/$($Event.max_retries)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "stream_event") {
                    $Inner = $Event.event

                    if (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_start" -and
                        $Inner.content_block.type -eq "tool_use"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host ""
                        Write-Host "[TOOL] $($Inner.content_block.name)" -ForegroundColor DarkCyan
                    }
                    elseif (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Claude returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }
                    else {
                        Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 2 repair completed" -ForegroundColor Green
                    }

                    if ($null -ne $Event.total_cost_usd) {
                        Write-Host "[USAGE] Cost: `$$($Event.total_cost_usd)"
                    }
                }
            }

        $ClaudeExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    }
    finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $PreviousErrorPreference
    }

    if ($ClaudeExit -ne 0) {
        throw "Stage 2 Sonnet repair failed with exit code $ClaudeExit. Raw log: $RawLog"
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Stage 2 repaired working tree:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    git status --short

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Real content changes:"
    git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --name-status

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 2 repair ready for final review." -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
}

        (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false))
    )

    Write-Host "[AGENT] Launching Claude Sonnet to build ALL Gauntlet phases" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
    Write-Host ""

    $PreviousErrorPreference = $ErrorActionPreference

    try {
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"

        Get-Content -LiteralPath $PromptPath -Raw -Encoding UTF8 |
            docker compose -p nosafecircle run --rm -T claude `
                claude -p `
                --model sonnet `
                --max-turns 120 `
                --permission-mode dontAsk `
                --output-format stream-json `
                --verbose `
                --include-partial-messages `
                --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write,Bash `
                --allowedTools Read Glob Grep Edit Write Bash `
                --disallowedTools NotebookEdit WebSearch WebFetch 2>&1 |
            Tee-Object -FilePath $RawLog |
            ForEach-Object {
                $Line = [string]$_

                try {
                    $Event = $Line | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
                }
                catch {
                    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Line)) {
                        Write-Host "[RAW] $Line" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
                    }
                    return
                }

                if ($Event.type -eq "system") {
                    if ($Event.subtype -eq "init") {
                        Write-Host "[AGENT] Claude session started" -ForegroundColor Cyan
                    }
                    elseif ($Event.subtype -eq "api_retry") {
                        Write-Host "[RETRY] API retry $($Event.attempt)/$($Event.max_retries)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "stream_event") {
                    $Inner = $Event.event

                    if (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_start" -and
                        $Inner.content_block.type -eq "tool_use"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host ""
                        Write-Host "[TOOL] $($Inner.content_block.name)" -ForegroundColor DarkCyan
                    }
                    elseif (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Gauntlet builder returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }
                    else {
                        Write-Host "[DONE] Gauntlet builder completed" -ForegroundColor Green
                    }

                    if ($null -ne $Event.total_cost_usd) {
                        Write-Host "[USAGE] Cost: `$$($Event.total_cost_usd)"
                    }
                }
            }

        $ClaudeExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    }
    finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $PreviousErrorPreference
    }

    if ($ClaudeExit -ne 0) {
        throw "Gauntlet builder failed with exit code $ClaudeExit. Raw log: $RawLog"
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Gauntlet builder history:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    git log --oneline --decorate -8

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Gauntlet builder checkout:"
    git status --short

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[DONE] Gauntlet build finished in isolated clone." -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
}

### Behavior

        --method PUT `
        "repos/$Repo/pulls/$PrNumber/merge" `
        -f "merge_method=merge" `
        -f "sha=$Stage2Head"

    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "GitHub rejected Stage 2 merge."
    }

    $Merge = $MergeJson | ConvertFrom-Json

    if (-not $Merge.merged) {
        throw "Stage 2 was not merged: $($Merge.message)"
    }

    $MergeSha = [string]$Merge.sha

    Write-Host "[PASS] Stage 2 merged" -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[STATE] Merge commit: $MergeSha"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Local main
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    git switch main
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Could not switch to main."
    }

    git pull --ff-only origin main
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Could not update local main."
    }

    git merge-base --is-ancestor $Stage2Head main
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Stage 2 commit is not contained in local main."
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "============================================================" -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[DONE] STAGE 2 IS IN MAIN" -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "============================================================" -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[STATE] Stage 2 head: $Stage2Head"
    Write-Host "[STATE] Merge commit: $MergeSha"
    Write-Host ""
    git status --short --branch
    git log --oneline --decorate -6
}

    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(
        $PromptPath,
        (($Prompt -replace "`r`n", "`n") -replace "`r", "`n"),
        (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false))
    )

    Write-Host "[AGENT] Launching Claude Sonnet for Stage 3" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
    Write-Host ""

    $PreviousErrorPreference = $ErrorActionPreference

    try {
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"

        Get-Content -LiteralPath $PromptPath -Raw -Encoding UTF8 |
            docker compose -p nosafecircle run --rm -T claude `
                claude -p `
                --model sonnet `
                --max-turns 100 `
                --permission-mode dontAsk `
                --output-format stream-json `
                --verbose `
                --include-partial-messages `
                --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write,Bash `
                --allowedTools Read Glob Grep Edit Write Bash `
                --disallowedTools NotebookEdit WebSearch WebFetch 2>&1 |
            Tee-Object -FilePath $RawLog |
            ForEach-Object {
                $Line = [string]$_

                try {
                    $Event = $Line | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
                }
                catch {
                    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Line)) {
                        Write-Host "[RAW] $Line" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
                    }
                    return
                }

                if ($Event.type -eq "system") {
                    if ($Event.subtype -eq "init") {
                        Write-Host "[AGENT] Claude session started" -ForegroundColor Cyan
                    }
                    elseif ($Event.subtype -eq "api_retry") {
                        Write-Host "[RETRY] API retry $($Event.attempt)/$($Event.max_retries)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "stream_event") {
                    $Inner = $Event.event

                    if (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_start" -and
                        $Inner.content_block.type -eq "tool_use"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host ""
                        Write-Host "[TOOL] $($Inner.content_block.name)" -ForegroundColor DarkCyan
                    }
                    elseif (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Claude returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }
                    else {
                        Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 3 implementation completed" -ForegroundColor Green
                    }

                    if ($null -ne $Event.total_cost_usd) {
                        Write-Host "[USAGE] Cost: `$$($Event.total_cost_usd)"
                    }
                }
            }

        $ClaudeExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    }
    finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $PreviousErrorPreference
    }

    if ($ClaudeExit -ne 0) {
        throw "Stage 3 Sonnet pass failed with exit code $ClaudeExit. Raw log: $RawLog"
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Stage 3 working tree:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    git status --short

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Real Stage 3 content changes:"
    git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --name-status

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 3 candidate ready for review." -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
}

+ task ID
+ attempt number

                    return
                }

                    if ($Event.subtype -eq "init") {
                        Write-Host "[AGENT] Claude session started" -ForegroundColor Cyan
                    }
                    elseif ($Event.subtype -eq "api_retry") {
                        Write-Host "[RETRY] API retry $($Event.attempt)/$($Event.max_retries)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "stream_event") {
                    $Inner = $Event.event

                    if (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_start" -and
                        $Inner.content_block.type -eq "tool_use"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host ""
                        Write-Host "[TOOL] $($Inner.content_block.name)" -ForegroundColor DarkCyan
                    }
                    elseif (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Fable review returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }
                    else {
                        Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 3 adversarial review completed" -ForegroundColor Green
                    }

                    if ($null -ne $Event.total_cost_usd) {
                        Write-Host "[USAGE] Cost: `$$($Event.total_cost_usd)"
                    }
                }
            }

        $ClaudeExit = $LASTEXITCODE

        $ErrorActionPreference = $PreviousErrorPreference

            Tee-Object -FilePath $RawLog |
            ForEach-Object {

                try {
                    $Event = $Line | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
                }
                catch {
                    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Line)) {
                        Write-Host "[RAW] $Line" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
                    }
                    return
                }

                if ($Event.type -eq "system") {
                    if ($Event.subtype -eq "init") {
                        Write-Host "[AGENT] Claude session resumed" -ForegroundColor Cyan
                    }
                    elseif ($Event.subtype -eq "api_retry") {
                        Write-Host "[RETRY] API retry $($Event.attempt)/$($Event.max_retries)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "stream_event") {
                    $Inner = $Event.event

                    if (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_start" -and
                        $Inner.content_block.type -eq "tool_use"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host ""
                        Write-Host "[TOOL] $($Inner.content_block.name)" -ForegroundColor DarkCyan
                    }
                    elseif (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Claude resume returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }
                    else {
                        Write-Host "[DONE] Final Stage 3 repair completed" -ForegroundColor Green
                    }

                    if ($null -ne $Event.total_cost_usd) {
                        Write-Host "[USAGE] Cost: `$$($Event.total_cost_usd)"
                    }
                }
            }

        $ClaudeExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    }
    finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $PreviousErrorPreference
    }

    if ($ClaudeExit -ne 0) {
        throw "Resumed Stage 3 repair failed with exit code $ClaudeExit. Raw log: $RawLog"
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Final Stage 3 candidate:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    git status --short

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Real content changes:"
    git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --name-status

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[DONE] Stage 3 resume finished." -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
}

    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(
        $PromptPath,
        (($Prompt -replace "`r`n", "`n") -replace "`r", "`n"),
        (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false))
    )

    Write-Host "[AGENT] Resuming the Sonnet session that built Gauntlet v1" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
    Write-Host ""

    $PreviousErrorPreference = $ErrorActionPreference

    try {
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"

        Get-Content -LiteralPath $PromptPath -Raw -Encoding UTF8 |
            docker compose -p nosafecircle run --rm -T claude `
                claude -p `
                --resume $SessionId `
                --model sonnet `
                --max-turns 140 `
                --permission-mode dontAsk `
                --output-format stream-json `
                --verbose `
                --include-partial-messages `
                --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write,Bash `
                --allowedTools Read Glob Grep Edit Write Bash `
                --disallowedTools NotebookEdit WebSearch WebFetch 2>&1 |
            Tee-Object -FilePath $RawLog |
            ForEach-Object {
                $Line = [string]$_

                try {
                    $Event = $Line | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
                }
                catch {
                    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Line)) {
                        Write-Host "[RAW] $Line" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
                    }
                    return
                }

                if ($Event.type -eq "system") {
                    if ($Event.subtype -eq "init") {
                        Write-Host "[AGENT] Gauntlet session resumed" -ForegroundColor Cyan
                    }
                    elseif ($Event.subtype -eq "api_retry") {
                        Write-Host "[RETRY] API retry $($Event.attempt)/$($Event.max_retries)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "stream_event") {
                    $Inner = $Event.event

                    if (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_start" -and
                        $Inner.content_block.type -eq "tool_use"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host ""
                        Write-Host "[TOOL] $($Inner.content_block.name)" -ForegroundColor DarkCyan
                    }
                    elseif (
                        $Inner.type -eq "content_block_delta" -and
                        $Inner.delta.type -eq "text_delta"
                    ) {
                        Write-Host $Inner.delta.text -NoNewline
                    }
                    elseif ($Inner.type -eq "message_stop") {
                        Write-Host ""
                    }
                }
                elseif ($Event.type -eq "result") {
                    Write-Host ""

                    if ($Event.is_error) {
                        Write-Host "[BLOCKED] Gauntlet v2 builder returned an error" -ForegroundColor Red
                    }
                    else {
                        Write-Host "[DONE] Gauntlet v2 builder completed" -ForegroundColor Green
                    }

                    if ($null -ne $Event.total_cost_usd) {
                        Write-Host "[USAGE] Cost: `$$($Event.total_cost_usd)"
                    }
                }
            }

        $ClaudeExit = $LASTEXITCODE
    }
    finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $PreviousErrorPreference
    }

    if ($ClaudeExit -ne 0) {
        throw "Gauntlet v2 builder failed with exit code $ClaudeExit. Raw log: $RawLog"
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Gauntlet v2 history:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    git log --oneline --decorate -10

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Real content changes from v1:"
    git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol $BackupBranch...HEAD --name-status

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[STATE] Current checkout:"
    git status --short

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[DONE] Gauntlet v2 build finished." -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "[LOG] $RawLog"
}

Tasks across groups are disjoint.

Do NOT represent these conflicts merely as dependencies.

Prefer separate output files so we test resource arbitration without intentionally generating textual Git merge conflicts.
